name: Reconstructed C2 store-residence #06

documented_range.note: Anonymous count-unit toward the July 1835 665-roof programme. No evidence establishes that this particular building existed, and no source names an occupant of this lot.

position.symbolic_location: Anonymous reconstructed roof in the South Division block bounded by South Water, Dearborn, Lake and Clark; standing ON the South Water Street frontage itself, one unit of the party-line row along it
position.note: PARTY-LINE FRONTAGE, DERIVED FROM THE COMMITTED PLAT (T-0078). This building does not stand centred on a lot at a typology setback: it stands ON the north face of blk_south_water_clark, the block's South Water Street frontage, whose line and bearing are read from the block boundary in data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json — the same committed geometry the lot grid and the corridor gate are derived from. Its front wall is 1.50 m back from that lot line, which is the closest line the plat module's own margin allows and is not a measurement of this frontage, and its east wall is fixed by the west wall of pruyne_kimball_drugstore, which it shares a party line with. The bearing is the face's own, so the front looks square at South Water Street. The run carries no lateral offset, because a shared party wall is one wall and cannot wander. WHAT IS INVENTED IS STILL EVERYTHING THAT MATTERS: that a building stood here at all, which building it was, and that these particular units stood shoulder to shoulder. What the 1834 South Water Street view supports is the TREATMENT — a continuous working row of party walls rather than detached cottages set back on grass. The treatment is what this placement takes from it, and a run standing on any other face of the town is borrowing it from that one street: the view draws a row, it does not place this row. Standing on a derived block face is not standing on a recovered lot, and the side lot lines this row crosses were always conjectural.

siding_exposure_m.note: INVENTED WITHIN A STOCK SET, NOT DERIVED. No source states the exposed face of any Chicago building's siding. The value is one of four period mill sidings — 4.5, 5, 5.5 or 6 in to the weather; this roof wears 6 in — dealt in this building's own parcel recipe: drawn from the set on this record's stable key, then advanced so that no roof of the parcel standing within 60 m hangs the same course. It is NOT keyed to a construction season the way the named buildings' stocks are: this record's 1835-01-01 is the programme's count-unit convention and not a date anything was built, so keying to it would deal every anonymous roof in the town one stock. The separation is the surface variety T-0049 reconstructs, not a claim about 1835. docs/LIBERTIES.md L148 owns the invention and the recipe half is recorded beside it, under `tools/siding_stock.py`.

occupants.note: SEATED BY THE STREET-FACE ADOPTION POLICY (docs/STREET-FACE-ADOPTION.md, the owner's ruling of 2026-08-29 for T-0354, extended 2026-08-30 for T-0416; liberty L212). The newspaper register places this business on South Water Street AND NOTHING NARROWER — 13 printings, 1833-12-03 to 1835-07-29, claims chicago_democrat_1833_12_03#c009, chicago_democrat_1834_02_25#c003, chicago_democrat_1834_03_04#c006, chicago_democrat_1834_04_01#c006, chicago_democrat_1834_04_16#c008, chicago_democrat_1834_04_30#c013, chicago_democrat_1834_06_04#c010, chicago_democrat_1834_06_11#c009, chicago_democrat_1834_06_18#c010, chicago_democrat_1834_07_02#c006, chicago_democrat_1835_06_04#c004, chicago_democrat_1835_07_22#c013, chicago_democrat_1835_07_29#c016 — so it takes the STREET FACE and not a lot. THE ROOF'S PLATTED LOT FACES South Water Street, which is the plat's own answer to which street it fronts. WHICH roof on that face it is given is an allocation by tools/adopt_street_faces.py and not a reading of any source, and nothing here says this business stood nearer the corner than any other on the same face. THE ROOF'S OWN EXISTENCE, POSITION AND FOOTPRINT REMAIN CONJECTURAL and are unchanged by the adoption: the business is documented, the building under it is not, and this attribute is graded `reconstructed` because the invented part is the whole of the placement.

frontage.why: T-0431, piece 3 of 4 of T-0420, and the ruling that made this ground workable at all. T-0143 and T-0188 each refused to tighten a party-line row against a street line that might move, and T-0317 inherited the refusal; T-0009 closed it on 2026-08-29 under the owner's ruling that the drawn South Water line does NOT move — the corridor was re-derived from committed control (`recentred`, +8.58 m) and data/streets/1835.json was not touched — so this face may carry a row again. THE ROW STILL STANDS ON THE BLOCK FACE AND NOT ON THAT CORRIDOR, which is the distinction the two refusals were protecting: the face is committed geometry read from data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json, and this run takes its line, its bearing and the end it packs back from off that boundary. The 8.58 m the corridor moved is therefore not in this placement, and if the strip between the corridor and the block faces is later resolved (T-0419) this roof does not move with it. THE FACE IS THIS BLOCK'S OWN RECORD RATHER THAN THE TOWN'S. tools/measure_street_frontage.py reads the two streets town-wide at South Water against Lake and does NOT make South Water the better face by the usual count; the reading that decides this parcel is the BLOCK's, where South Water carries four documented records — Harmon & Loomis's store, Pruyne & Kimball's drug store, John Bates Jr.'s auction room and Madore Beaubien's house — against Lake's one, the first Tremont House. Three of those four are commercial. That is the face a store belongs on here, and T-0024's second clause puts a commercial roof ON the street line rather than back at a dwelling's setback. THE END RULE AGREES AND IS READ RATHER THAN ASSERTED: tools/measure_end_rule.py blk_south_water_clark --list puts lot 2 at 84.44 m walked from the foot of the Dearborn Street drawbridge — the only crossing of the main stem in July 1835 — against 231.87 m for lot 1, the block's other free lot. The face grades on the walked criterion at a 6.07 m unit step and is BELOW THE FLOOR at 4.81 m on T-A11's straight line, so the walk is what makes any grading of this face possible, exactly as it was on blk_randolph_market. NO COORDINATE IS AUTHORED: the line, its bearing and the lot's own stretch of it are read from the committed block boundary, and the 1.5 m setback is the plat module's own lot margin rather than a measurement of this frontage. WHAT IS INVENTED IS STILL EVERYTHING THAT MATTERS: that a building stood on this ground at all, that it was a store, and that it shared a wall with the drug store beside it.
